actions.text: Accepted with all three metrics improved. Submitting.

actions.reason: secp256r1/src/field.rs: invert_canonical now computes Kaliski's almost inverse x = a^-1 * 2^k mod p (256 <= k <= 512) instead of the binary extended GCD with a modular halving per shifted bit. The invariant p = u*s + v*r keeps r and s at most p, so the loop only uses plain shifts and additions without modular correction; only the final doubling is reduced once. FieldElement::invert folds the 2^-k correction into the Montgomery multiplication it already performed (multiplying by 2^(512-k) instead of R2, with 2^256 replaced by its residue NEG_MODULUS), so the result is the same field element. The now-unused sub_mod helper is replaced by shl1_limbs. Measured: scalar_mul_ir ratio 0.9695, msm_ir 0.9822, decode_ir 0.9652, outputs identical.

worker_outcome: submitted a perf candidate on scalar_mul_ir (77 changed lines); it was committed and revealed (status queued); its verdict comes later from independent replays [stop: submitted; model calls: 17]

journal.text: I first edited secp256r1/src/group.rs around lines 424-436 and then reverted it. Next I changed field.rs lines 270-278 alone. Evaluation 1 rejected it: scalar_mul_ir went 252121129 to 256031580, ratio 1.0155 against the required 0.9900. That change did not help. I then rewrote invert_canonical in field.rs as Kaliski's almost inverse, x = a^-1 * 2^k mod p with 256 <= k <= 512, in place of binary extended GCD with a modular halving per shifted bit. The invariant p = u*s + v*r keeps r and s at most p, so the loop uses plain shifts and adds, and only the final doubling is reduced. FieldElement::invert folds the 2^k factor back out. Evaluation 3 accepted it. scalar_mul_ir ratio 0.9695, msm_ir 0.9822, decode_ir 0.9652. Outputs were identical, 77 lines changed. It is submitted and queued for replay. I now think inversion cost shows up in all three metrics, decode most. Next I want to profile what remains in scalar_mul besides inversion, and check how batch_normalize calls invert.
